s: The left bar is your library, the top bar holds your open tabs, and the main area shows the page you are on.
x: Quick links on the left jump between Dashboard, All notes, Calendar, Tasks, Files, Whiteboards, Databases (when switched on) and Insights. Folders sit below the quick links as a real tree. Drag a page or folder onto another folder to move it. Search (Ctrl+K) finds pages, folders and app pages; Recent (Ctrl+R) shows what you opened lately. The ••• menu at the top right changes with what you are looking at: a page, a folder, or an app page.

s: The Dashboard lists a few things worth trying; each line does the thing and ticks itself off.
x: Click a line to do it (write a note, add a task, open the daily note, try the command bar, look at the calendar, import, choose a look). Hide it when you’re done; ••• is not needed — press Ctrl+Shift+P and choose “Show the Get started checklist again” to bring it back.

s: The bell in the top bar gathers what is overdue, due today, starting soon, due for review or ending.
x: Click the bell for the list: overdue and due-today tasks, meetings starting within three hours, reminders, pages due for review, a sprint about to end, and tasks blocked by others. Click an item to go straight to it. The red number counts the urgent ones.

s: Ctrl+Shift+P: type what you want to do instead of hunting for it.
x: Press Ctrl+Shift+P (or type > at the start of the search box) and start typing: “new task”, “go to calendar”, “theme”, “archive”… Use ↑ ↓ and Enter. Recently used commands are listed first when the box is empty. While a page is open the bar also offers actions for that page: properties, versions, reminder, move, duplicate, archive, favourite…

s: Everything is stored on your computer as plain files — nothing is uploaded.
x: Open Settings → Your files to see the folder and open it. Notes, folders, tasks, calendars, databases and whiteboards are small JSON files; documents you edit in Page view are saved as .docx files. To back up or move to another computer, copy that folder and put it back in the same place.

s: Pick a light, dark or coloured theme.
x: Open ••• → Themes, or Settings → Appearance. Choose a theme; it applies everywhere without moving anything.

t: Make Doceo easier to read and use
s: Larger text, higher contrast, a simpler screen, a readable font and bigger buttons.
x: Open Settings → Accessibility. Text size makes the sidebar, tabs and pages larger (Standard, Large, Larger, Largest). Documents keep their own zoom. Contrast darkens secondary text and firms up lines. Simple view hides shortcut hints, tips and decoration. Readable font and Line spacing make text easier to follow; Buttons and rows makes targets bigger; Focus outline makes the keyboard position unmistakable; Motion → Reduced stops animations (your system’s Reduce motion setting is also honoured). Autosave is always on: notes, pages, slides and sheets save a moment after you stop typing.

s: Deleted notes wait in the Trash until you restore them or empty it.
x: Open Trash from the sidebar (the bin icon). Click a note to preview it; Restore brings it back, the bin button deletes it for good. Right-click Trash in the sidebar → Open trash, Restore all notes or Empty trash. The round button at the bottom right empties the whole trash after you confirm — it can’t be undone.

s: Open several pages at once and jump between them.
x: Click a page to open it in a tab; the + asks which kind to make (Note, Page, Slides or Sheet, or a template). Right-click a tab to open it beside the current one (split view). Drag a tab to reorder it, or pull it out of the strip to open it in its own window; drop it back on the strip to dock it again. Ctrl+W closes a tab. Alt+← / Alt+→ moves the focused tab. Settings → Tabs & navigation puts the breadcrumbs under the tabs or in the top bar.

s: Notes for thinking, Pages for documents, Slides for presenting, Sheets for numbers. All four live in All docs, in folders, and on every page that lists documents.
x: New (top left) or the + button creates any kind; folders can hold all four. On All docs, the pills Notes · Pages · Slides · Sheets filter the library; each kind has its own icon and tile shape. Pages, Slides and Sheets are stored as real .docx, .pptx and .xlsx files, so they open in other apps too. Open a .docx, .pptx or .xlsx from the Files page to edit it in place; Save writes back to the same file.

s: A gallery of ready-made starting points for every kind.
x: Press Ctrl+Shift+N, or New → From template…, or use the Create button on All docs. Pick Notes, Pages, Slides or Sheets (Alt+1 to Alt+4), search, and press Enter or click a card. Pages: letter, résumé, report, handbook, project proposal, meeting minutes, one-page brief, press release, procedure, weekly report. Slides: briefing, lesson, pitch, field notes, quarterly report, evening talk. Sheets: household budget, quarterly sales, gradebook, project tracker, invoice, weekly timesheet, habit tracker. Everything in a template is ordinary content — change it freely. Save your own note templates from

s: Type like in a word processor; the panel on the right holds styles, fonts, paragraph, insert, page setup, review and view.
x: Click the page and type. Use the toolbar for style, font, size, bold, lists and colours. Open the panel (right icon in the toolbar) → Page for paper size, orientation and margins; Insert for tables, pictures, headers, footers and page numbers. Ctrl+F finds text; Review has spelling, comments and tracked changes. ••• → Export as… saves a PDF, Word, Markdown, HTML or text copy wherever you choose.

s: A slide rail on the left, the slide in the middle, speaker notes underneath and a panel on the right.
x: Click + New slide (or the arrow beside it for a layout). Click a slide in the rail to edit it; drag to reorder. Click on the slide to select; double-click text to type. Drag handles to resize. Insert shapes, pictures, tables and charts from the toolbar. Design tab: themes and variants. Motion tab: transitions and animations. Press Present (or F5) for the slide show: arrows or click to advance, Esc to leave. Write speaker notes in the pane below the slide. ••• → Download as PowerPoint… or Export as PDF… saves a copy wherever you choose.

s: A grid with a formula bar, sheet tabs, a status-bar summary and a panel with every spreadsheet command.
x: Click a cell and type; Tab and Enter commit and move. = starts a formula; the formula bar suggests functions. Drag the fill handle (the small square at a selection’s corner) to copy or continue a series; drag column and row edges to resize, double-click to fit. Select cells, then Insert → Chart. Click a chart to move it; the panel has chart design. Home has number formats, borders, fills and conditional formatting; Data has sorting, filters and validation (drop-down lists); Insert → Checkbox makes tick boxes. The status bar shows the sum, average and count of what is selected. The slider sets

t: Split view: two or three documents side by side
s: Read one document while you write in another, like editor groups in VS Code.
x: Open two or more documents, then press the split button at the right of the tab strip (or Ctrl+\). The most recent other tab appears beside the current one. With only one tab open it asks which document to put beside it. Or right-click a tab → “Open beside the current document”. Each pane has a coloured bar and a number; the tabs showing in a pane carry the same colour and number, so you can see which tabs belong together. The pane you last clicked is the active one — the toolbar, breadcrumbs and ••• menu follow it. Drag the divider between panes to resize it (or focus it and press ← →). Click

s: Red dotted lines mark spelling, blue ones grammar; right-click for suggestions. Typos fix themselves as you type.
x: In Notes, a misspelt word gets a red dotted underline and repeated words, a missing capital or “a/an” mistakes get a blue dotted one. Right-click the word (or press Alt+Enter with the cursor in it): its fixes appear at the top of the one menu — click a suggestion to replace the word, or choose Ignore all / Add to dictionary. Click anywhere else, or press Esc, to close it. Slides and Sheets show the same fixes when you right-click a word you are typing in a text box or a cell. AutoCorrect works when you finish a word: common typos (teh → the), a lone i → I, and a capital letter at the start of

t: Open a file with another app
s: Right-click a file or document to open it with any app that can read it.
x: On the Files page, right-click a file → Open, or Open with and pick an app from the list (macOS and Linux list the apps that can open that type; Windows opens its own “Open with” window). “Choose another app…” always works. Files that Doceo can’t edit (images, archives, code…) open in the app your system uses for them when you click them. Right-click a Page, Slides or Sheet in the library → “Open a copy with…”. It opens a copy of the file in the other app; what you save there does not come back into Doceo.

s: Open any document in its own window; edits save by themselves.
x: Pull a tab out of the tab strip to open that document in its own window; drop it back on the strip to dock it. Pages, Slides and Sheets save into your library a moment after you stop typing (Autosave is always on). A document opened from the Files page is a draft until you press Ctrl+S, which writes the original file. Closing a tab with unsaved changes to a file asks Save / Don’t save / Cancel.

t: Notes and Pages are different documents
s: A Note is a quick, flowing page for ideas; a Page is a real document with margins, headers and page numbers. They are separate kinds — nothing switches by itself.
x: Create either from New (top of the left bar) or the + button: Note, Page, Slides or Sheet. To turn a Note into a Page, use “Convert to a Page…” in the note’s File menu or panel; a Page has “Convert to a Note” in its panel. Each conversion makes a separate document. Pages are saved as real .docx files, so Word, Pages and Google Docs can open them.

s: The floating toolbar has everything: styles, font, size, bold, italic, lists, colours, links, tables and pictures.
x: Select text and use the toolbar, or right-click for a menu with size, colour, highlight and alignment. With nothing selected, choosing a font or size sets the page default. Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+K (link), Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y work as usual.

s: Type / at the start of a line to insert headings, lists, checklists, tables, columns, panels, code, diagrams, embeds and live blocks.
x: Type / then a few letters to filter (for example “table” or “database”). Use ↑ ↓ and Enter to insert, Esc to close.

s: Type [[ to link to another page, or @ to mention a page or a person.
x: Type [[ and pick a page — or choose “Create …” to make a new one on the spot. A link always shows the page’s current title. Under every page, “Linked from” and “Links to” list its backlinks.

t: Panels, columns, folding sections and more
s: Callout panels (info, note, success, warning, danger, decision), two or three columns, folding sections, a live contents list, code blocks and Mermaid diagrams.
x: Insert them from the / menu. A code block has a language picker; choose “mermaid” to draw a diagram from text. A “Contents” block lists the page’s headings and updates as you write.

s: Drag, align and wrap tables and pictures; paste screenshots straight in.
x: Insert a table from the toolbar or the / menu; use the small toolbar that appears to add or remove rows and columns. Paste an image, or drop a file: it is stored inside the page. Drag a picture to move it; text wraps around it. Use its toolbar for alignment and wrapping.

s: Select text and comment on it; reply, resolve or delete from the thread.
x: Select text, then press Ctrl+Alt+M (or Insert → Comment). Click the highlighted text to open the thread.

s: Search inside a page, or across all your pages.
x: Ctrl+F searches the page you are on (case, whole word and regular expressions are options). Ctrl+Shift+H finds and replaces across every page. Tick which pages to change; a version of each is saved first.

s: Make a page “a Meeting” or “a Person” so it gets its own fields and starting template.
x: Create a type from Databases → New type… (or Ctrl+Shift+P → “New type”): pick a starting point — Person, Meeting, Book, Project, Idea or blank — then name it and choose an icon and colour. Give a page a type with “+ Type” under its title (or Ctrl+Shift+P → “Page: make it a …”). Its fields appear under the title and are saved with the page; a page can have several types. Ctrl+Shift+P → “New Meeting” (etc.) starts a new page from the type’s template and name pattern (“Meeting — {date}”). Databases → Types lists every type with its pages as a table, board and more. Search with is:meeting to find

s: Write something once and show — and edit — it on as many pages as you like.
x: Type /synced block for a new one, or /existing synced block to show one you made before (the list says how many pages use each). Or select text and right-click → Make this a synced block: it moves into a synced block and the same block can then be used elsewhere. Edit it on any page and every page that shows it changes at once. The header says how many pages use it. Unsync turns this copy into ordinary text (other pages keep the block); Remove takes it off this page but keeps the block. Exports and Page view write out the block’s current text. Tasks inside a synced block aren’t listed on the T

s: Put a named value in a sentence — Budget: 1200 — and let search and lists read it.
x: Type Budget:: (the word, two colons and a space) and press Space: it becomes a small field; type the value and press Enter. Or type /field. Click either half of the field to change the name or the value; Esc puts it back. Search for it: field:budget finds pages that have it, field:status=done matches a value, field:budget>1000 compares numbers or dates (also <, >=, <=). A search-results block shows the field’s value beside every page it finds. In Markdown files a field is written Budget:: 1200 (or [Budget:: 1200] inside a sentence) — the same as Obsidian’s Dataview.

s: Live blocks that show a search, or part of another page, inside a page.
x: Type /search results, then a search: words and operators such as label:design is:favourite in:Work -draft. Add type:task to list tasks. It updates by itself. Type /embed, choose a page and (optionally) one of its sections: the content is shown here, read-only, and follows the original — use Open to edit it there. Both are written out as plain text when you export or switch to Page view.

s: Give a page labels and properties, then find pages by them.
x: Click “Add properties & labels” under the title (or ••• → Properties & labels…). Status can be Draft, In review, Approved or Archived. Add an owner and a date. Click a label anywhere to see every page that carries it.

s: Start a page from meeting notes, a project plan, a decision record, a retrospective, a weekly review or a spec.
x: Press Ctrl+Shift+N, or use + → From template. To keep your own: ••• → Save as template… . It then shows in the template picker.

s: Nest pages under pages, and attach files to a page.
x: ••• → Add child page, or Alt-drop a page onto another page in the left bar. Attach files from the Attachments box under a page; they stay with it.

s: Doceo keeps earlier versions of every page.
x: ••• → Version history… lists them. Restoring saves the current text first, so you can always come back. “Save a version now” in that window keeps one on purpose.

t: Embeds, link cards and live blocks
s: Videos, designs, issues, other pages’ lists, calendars, task boards and databases can live inside a page.
x: Paste a link to YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Figma, Google Docs / Sheets / Slides, or a GitHub issue to embed it; any other link on its own line becomes a preview card. Live blocks update by themselves: pages with a label, child pages, a properties report, a project’s tasks, an agenda, a task board and a database view (/database). Live blocks are written out as plain text and tables when you export or switch to Page view.

s: Paper size, orientation, margins, page numbers, headers and footers.
x: In Page view open the Format panel (toolbar, right side) → Page. Pick paper size, orientation and margins; insert page numbers and edit the header and footer.

s: Everything for the document — text, insert, page, review and view — in a side panel.
x: Open it with the panel button in the toolbar. Use Ctrl+/ to search every command by name.

t: Opening a file from your computer
s: Open .docx, .odt, .rtf, .html, .md, .txt or .tex files in place and save them back.
x: Press Ctrl+O, or use Files → Open file… (or Open folder… for a whole folder). Your edits are kept as a draft; Ctrl+S writes them back to the original file. Closing a tab with unsaved changes asks Save / Don’t save / Cancel. An old .doc file is saved as a .docx beside it and the original is left alone. PDFs open in a viewer (view only).

s: Save a page as PDF, Word, Markdown, HTML, RTF, OpenDocument, plain text or LaTeX.
x: ••• menu → Export, then pick a format. A Save dialog asks where; the file is written exactly there. Files → Exports lists everything you exported, with Open, Show in folder and Remove from list.

t: Unsorted, Favourites and other views of All notes
s: All notes is the one place for your whole library: folders, loose pages, favourites and more, chosen with the pills above the list.
x: All shows your folders and the pages that are in no folder; Folders shows only folders. Unsorted shows the pages that are in no folder. “Organise” (the round button) moves them into a folder in one go. Favourites gathers every page you starred, from any folder: right-click a page → Add to favourites, or use ••• while it is open. A ★ marks them everywhere. Daily notes and With tasks appear when you have some: every daily note, and every page that still has unticked checklist items. Inside a folder the pills are All, Folders, Notes and Favourites for that folder.

s: Drag and drop between the left bar and the dashboard, or use Move to… / Copy to….
x: Drag a page or folder onto a folder to move it; drop between items to reorder. Drop onto another page to group two pages into a new folder (Alt-drop nests a page under a page). Right-click anything for rename, colour, duplicate, move, copy and delete.

s: Give folders and pages a colour so they stand out in the left bar and the dashboard.
x: Right-click → Set colour (or ••• → Set colour while a page is open).

s: Deleted pages go to the Trash; archived pages are hidden but kept.
x: Delete moves a page (or a folder and its pages) to the Trash. Open Trash to Restore or Delete forever. ••• → Archive page hides a page from lists; show archived pages with the “Archived” pill, or restore it from the same menu. Dragging onto the Trash row also deletes.

s: See your pages as a sortable table and change many at once.
x: On All notes, a folder, a label or Recent switch to the table view. Tick pages to move them, add a label, set a status, merge them into one or send them to the trash.

s: A top-level folder shows a front page with a description, counts, recent updates, labels and projects.
x: Open a top-level folder and click “Add a description” to write one. Export links on that page save the folder as Markdown, HTML or a website.

s: Ctrl+K searches titles, labels, owners and the text of every page, plus tasks, whiteboards and app pages.
x: Type to search; use the filters for label, folder, status, owner and modified date. Tick “Archived” to include archived pages.

s: Narrow a search by typing operators — click one under the search box to insert it.
x: label:design (or #design) · in:Work (a folder or parent page) · status:draft · owner:sam · is:favourite · is:daily · is:task (pages with open checklist items) · is:unsorted · is:archived has:reminder · before:2026-10-01 · after:2026-01-01 · edited:week (day, week or month) · type:task (or page, folder, board) “exact phrase” keeps words together; -word leaves out pages that contain it. ☆ Save this search keeps it as a chip above the results for next time.

s: See how your notes connect.
x: Ctrl+Shift+P → “Open the graph…”, or Insights → Graph. Every page with a [[link]] (or a child page) is a dot; bigger dots have more links. Hover to highlight a page’s neighbours, click to open it, scroll to zoom and drag to move around. Find a page by name, show only one type, or include pages with no links.

s: See which pages need attention (the Insights page in the left bar).
x: Insights lists pages that need review, are stale (90+ days), most viewed, never opened, have broken [[links]] or stand alone. In a page’s properties set “Review every N months”; “Mark verified” resets the clock.

s: One page per day in a “Daily notes” folder, started with a Plan checklist and a Notes section.
x: Press Ctrl+J (or click “Daily note” in the left bar) to open today’s page — it is created the first time. Unfinished checklist items from your last daily note are carried over into today’s Plan. In Calendar, right-click a day → Open daily note to start or open any other day.

s: Ctrl+Shift+Space opens a small box from anywhere in the app.
x: Type your thought and choose where it goes: Today’s note (a timed bullet), Task, or New page. Press Enter to save, Shift+Enter for a new line, Esc to cancel. For a task you can use the same shortcuts as the board: “Call the bank fri 3pm !high #Home”. The last destination you chose is remembered.

s: Every task has one card; look at your work the way that suits you.
x: Overview shows projects and progress; Board has To do / In progress / In review / Done columns — drag cards between them. List, Table and Timeline show the same tasks; on the timeline drag a bar to move it and its ends to resize it. Dates are shared with the Calendar.

s: Type a sentence and Doceo picks out the date, time, priority, project and document.
x: Click + in a column (or “New task”) and type, for example: Send report fri 3pm !high #Website @Spec !high / !med / !low sets priority; #Name picks a project; @Name links a document; words like “tomorrow”, “fri” or “3pm” set the date and time. Ctrl+Shift+Space adds a task from anywhere.

s: Tick items in any note and they appear on the board, too.
x: Insert a checklist from the / menu. Open an item from the board to add a due date, priority, comments or documents — it is saved back into the note.

s: Group tasks into projects; park ideas in the Backlog; finished work is archived automatically.
x: Press + beside Projects in the left bar; double-click or use ⋯ to rename, recolour or delete (tasks are kept). The Backlog holds work you have not committed to; show it as a board column with the Backlog pill. Finished tasks move to the Archive after the number of days set in Settings → Tasks (0 = never); reopen them from there.

s: Tasks in a project get a number like APP-12; mark a task as a Bug, Story or Epic and group tasks under an epic.
x: Each project has a key (from its name). Right-click the project → Ticket key… to change it. New tasks are numbered APP-1, APP-2… and keep their number. Open a task and choose its Type; an epic’s drawer lists its tasks with progress. Set a task’s Epic from its drawer; filter by epic from “Epics” in the left bar.

s: Say what blocks a task, what it duplicates or what it relates to.
x: Open a task → Linked tasks → pick the kind of link → Link a task. The other task shows the opposite wording (“Is blocked by”). A task whose blocker is not finished shows a red “Blocked” badge.

s: Plan work in time-boxes with a goal, dates, progress and a burndown.
x: Press + beside Sprints in the left bar to add one (two weeks by default). Put tasks in it with the Sprint field in a task’s drawer. Select the sprint to see its panel: edit name, dates and goal, then Start sprint. Only one sprint per project is active. Complete sprint asks what to do with unfinished tasks: move them to the backlog, the next sprint, or leave them without a sprint.

s: Finish a repeating task and the next one appears, due on its next date.
x: Open a task → Repeat, and choose every day, weekday, week, 2 weeks, month or year — or type it when you add the task: “Water plants every 2 weeks”, “Standup every weekday”, “Gym every mon wed fri”. When you tick it done a new copy is made (checklist reset) with the next due date; it never lands in the past if you were late. Tick “after done” to count the next one from the day you finished instead of from the due date.

t: Estimates, custom fields and child tasks
s: Story points, your own fields per project, and sub-tasks that are real tasks.
x: Open a task → Estimate to give it points; sprints show finished / planned points and the Table view has a Points column. Right-click a project → Custom fields… to add text, number, choice, date or checkbox fields; every task in the project then shows them in its drawer, and the Table view gets a column for each. In a task’s drawer, “Child tasks” makes tasks that belong to it, each with its own status, date and assignee; the parent shows how many are done. (“Subtasks” below it are a simple checklist.) Deleting a parent keeps its children.

t: Swimlanes, work-in-progress limits, bulk edit and templates
s: Tune the board for bigger projects.
x: Above the board choose Swimlanes: None, Person, Priority, Epic or Project. Drag cards between columns inside a lane; click a lane’s title to fold it. Click the number on a column header to set a work-in-progress limit; the column turns red when it holds more. Select lets you tick several cards, then change status, priority, project or sprint for all of them, archive them or delete them. Open a task → Save as template to keep its shape (title, description, checklist, tags, type, estimate, repeat); Templates above the board starts a new task from one.

s: See how much gets finished and where work piles up.
x: Tasks → Reports: tasks open, overdue, finished this week and month, and the typical time from creating a task to finishing it. Velocity compares planned and finished work (points, or tasks) for your last sprints; “Created vs finished” and “Open work over time” cover the last 30 days. Workload shows open tasks per person (red when some are overdue); Age of open work shows how long things have been waiting. Reports follow the project and person you have selected in the left bar. They count board tasks (checklist items in notes have no created or finished time).

s: Rules that do routine things for you while Doceo is open.
x: Tasks → Automations (above the board). Start from a ready-made rule — finish a parent when its child tasks are done, new bugs become high priority, overdue work gets noticed, started work joins the active sprint — or build your own. A rule is: when (a task is created · moves to a status · becomes overdue · all its child tasks are done), only if (project, type, priority, tag), then actions (set status or priority, add a tag, assign, set a due date, put in the active sprint, add a child task, comment, tell me). The switch on each rule pauses it. Every change a rule makes is written in the task’s

s: Keep a filtered view in the left bar.
x: Choose filters (list, project, document, tag, priority, person, epic, sprint, search). Press + beside Saved filters and name it; click it later to apply it, ✕ to delete.

s: Bring in a Jira CSV export; nothing is sent back to Jira.
x: In Jira: search for issues → Export → CSV (all fields). In Doceo: Tasks → the import icon in the top bar → choose the file. Check the summary and press Import. Keys, types, epics, sub-tasks, comments, labels and sprints come across; importing the same file again skips issues you already have.

s: Group finished work into versions; the changelog and a public roadmap page write themselves.
x: Tasks → Releases in the left bar → +. Name it (v1.1), give it a target date and a few words of release notes. Put tasks in it from the task’s Release field, or with Select → Release… on the board. Press Release when it ships: it is dated today, and unfinished tasks go to the backlog, another release, or nowhere — you choose. Changelog saves a Markdown file (Highlights · New · Improved · Fixed, from each task’s type); Public page saves one self-contained HTML file with the roadmap by quarter and the changelog. Upload it wherever you like — Doceo hosts nothing.

s: New tasks that still need a project, a priority or a date wait here for a once-over.
x: Tasks → Triage in the left bar (the number is how many are waiting). Fill in the missing project, priority, person or date — a task leaves the list when it has them all — or press Accept to take it as it is, or To backlog to park it. Tasks stop appearing here two weeks after they were made.

s: Name a project’s stages your way, switch off stages it doesn’t use, and set rules for moving work along.
x: Right-click a project in the left bar → Workflow…. Rename the stages (To do → Ready…) and tick “Not used” for In progress or In review if you don’t need them; To do and Done always stay. Choose “Stage by stage” to stop tasks jumping ahead (going back is always allowed), and tick what a task needs before it can be Done — a due date, a person, an estimate, a description. The board for that project shows your names; a move that breaks a rule is refused with a short reason. Reset to default undoes it all.

s: All your projects at a glance, who has too much on, and a written update for each project.
x: Tasks → Reports shows a Portfolio card (when you have more than one project): progress, what is overdue, the next release and the active sprint — a red bar means overdue work or a late release. Press Update beside a project to post a status update: pick on track, at risk or off track and edit the drafted text. Earlier updates are listed and can be copied as Markdown. Capacity shows each person’s open points (or tasks) by due week. Type a weekly capacity beside a name and weeks over it turn red, near it amber. Burnup shows scope against finished work; Cumulative flow shows where tasks sat each

s: See which task blocks which.
x: Mark a task as blocking another (task → Linked tasks → blocks). On the Timeline a line runs from the blocker’s end to the blocked task’s start; it turns red when the blocked task is scheduled to start too early. Use the Dependencies button above the timeline to hide the lines.

s: A goal has key results; its progress is their average.
x: Open Goals in the left bar → New goal. Add key results: a Number result (from, now, target — update “now” as you go) or one From a project’s tasks (progress is the share of that project’s tasks that are done). Give it a period like 2026-Q4 (or H1 2027, or 2026) and its dates fill in. A goal with no key results has a progress slider. The badge says how it is doing against the clock: On track (within 10 points of where it should be), At risk (within 25), Off track, or Done.

s: Sort goals into what you are working on, what is next and what is for later.
x: Choose Now · Next · Later at the top of Goals. Move a goal between columns with the arrows (or the “When” menu on the goal). On a quarter’s page, “Plan 2027-Q1” starts the next quarter’s first goal.

s: Day, work week, week, month and agenda.
x: Month scrolls continuously; Day, Work week and Week page sideways with a swipe. Keys: ← → previous / next, T today, D / W / M / 5 / A choose the view.

s: Drag on the grid to create; drag to move; drag an edge to resize.
x: Right-click a time → New event here (or New all-day event). Double-click an event to see its details; Edit changes it. Hold Alt (Option) while dragging to copy. Events can repeat, carry a link, people, notes and a Doceo note (Take notes creates a meeting page).

s: Subscribe to a calendar link, or sign in with Microsoft 365.
x: Add calendar → Microsoft 365 / Teams to sign in (read only), or paste an ICS link (Outlook “Publish calendar”, Google secret iCal address, iCloud webcal). Feeds refresh automatically (and with Refresh now). Their events are read only; dragging one makes a local copy. Your responses (accept / tentative / decline) are saved in Doceo only — nothing is sent back.

s: Databases is opt-in.
x: Settings → Features → Databases → Show. A Databases row then appears in the left bar.

s: Start from a template (task tracker, reading list, content calendar, roadmap, blank) and choose which pages it covers.
x: Open Databases and click a template tile. Rows are real pages. Use the scope selector to cover all pages, one folder or one label. “New page” adds a row (and a page).

s: Text, number, select, multi-select, date, person, link, checkbox, email, phone, page properties, relations, rollups and formulas.
x: Press + at the right end of the header to add a column; click a column title for its menu. Page-property columns (status, owner, date, labels, created, modified, folder) are shared with the page itself. Relations link two databases; rollups summarise related pages (count, sum, average, earliest…).

s: Save as many views as you like on one database.
x: Table, Board, Gallery, List, Calendar and Timeline are the layouts; the + beside the tabs adds a view. Filter, Sort and Group are on the bar; Properties hides columns. Drag cards between board lanes, chips between calendar days and bars on the timeline.

s: A formula column calculates from the other columns of the same row.
x: Add a column of type Formula and write an expression such as: prop("Estimate") * 100 + if(prop("Done"), 1, 0) prop("Column") reads a column; use + − × ÷, comparisons, if / ifs, text, list, number and date functions (the column menu lists them all). A mistake shows “⚠ Error” in the cell with the reason on hover — nothing else breaks.

t: Looking in other databases from a formula
s: A formula can read rows of another database by its name — no relation needed.
x: lookup("Customers", "Code", prop("Customer"), "Plan") finds the first row of Customers whose Code equals this row’s Customer and gives its Plan. countIf("Orders", "Customer", prop("Code")), sumIf(…, "Amount") and averageIf(…) count, add up and average over the matching rows; column("Orders", "Amount") gives a whole column as a list for sum(), average() or join(). Names and values ignore capital letters. A database or column that doesn’t exist is named in the error; two databases that look at each other stop with an error instead of looping.

s: See how many pages (or how much) are in each group — as bars, columns, a line, a pie or one big number.
x: Press + beside the view tabs and choose Chart (or change a view’s layout to Chart). Pick the kind of chart, what to group by (a choice, labels, a person, a date by day / week / month / year…) and whether to count pages or add up, average or find the smallest / largest of a number column. The chart follows the view’s filters, so “Open bugs by severity” is a filter plus a chart. For a dashboard, make a page and type /database several times: choose the database and its chart view in each block (the block’s + Chart button adds one). The blocks stay up to date and become tables when you export.

s: Add pages the same way every time: a form with only the columns you want, and templates that fill in the values.
x: Add a Form view (+ beside the view tabs). It shows a title and the columns that are visible in the view — use Properties to choose them. Press the button to add a page; choose whether the form clears or opens the new page afterwards. Templates (on the bar) hold starting values, a title like “Bug {date}” and, if you like, the content of a page you copy. “New page” asks which template to start from; a form can use one too. Templates never change pages that already exist.

s: Themes across quarters, or Now / Next / Later — drag a card to reschedule it.
x: Add a view (+ beside the view tabs) and choose Roadmap. Lanes = a Select column such as Theme or Team (or None). Columns = Quarters from a date column, or Stages from a Select column such as Horizon (Now / Next / Later). Drag a card to another quarter to change its date, to another lane to re-file it. “Earlier” and “Later” show pages outside the window; “No date” holds the rest.

s: Rank ideas with RICE, ICE, value ÷ effort or your own weights, and see them on a 2×2 grid.
x: Press Score on the database bar, pick a method and which columns feed it; Doceo adds a Score column. Add a Matrix view: pick the number columns across (effort) and up (value). Drag a dot to change its two numbers; the four corners are labelled quick wins, big bets, fill-ins and money pits. Ideas & feedback (a starter on the Databases page) links feedback to ideas, counts votes and mentions, scores them with RICE and has a button that promotes an idea to an epic.

s: A button that sets a column, adds a task or opens a page — in every row, or in the middle of a page.
x: Database: add a column of type Button, then open its menu to choose the text and what it does to that row. Page: type /button, then click ✎ to set it up. Actions: set a column to a value, set a date to today / tomorrow / next week, add or remove a label, add a task (with a project, due date and priority), add a page to a database, open a page, or show a message. In text, {title} is the row’s title and {Column name} is any of its values. A button in a page can say which database the page is a row of, so it can set that row’s columns.

s: Rules that act on a database’s pages while Doceo is open.
x: Open a database and press Automations → New rule. Choose what starts it: a page is added, a column changes (optionally to a particular value), or a date column is reached (that day, or some days before / after). Optionally add a condition (Stage is Open…), then choose the actions — the same ones buttons use. Rules never run for pages that were already there when Doceo opened, a missed date is caught for a day, and rules that keep setting each other off are paused for a moment.

s: Change many rows at once, save a view as CSV, or put a view inside a page.
x: Tick rows to set one column on all of them or move them to the trash. The download button in the header saves the visible columns as a CSV file. In any page type /database, then choose the database and view; Open jumps to it.

s: Shapes, sticky notes, text, images, arrows, a pen, page cards and task cards.
x: Open Whiteboards and create a board; drag shapes from the panel onto the canvas. Hover a shape and drag from a port to connect it with a line; click a quick-add arrow to clone and connect in one go. Group (Ctrl+G), align, distribute, add layers and pages; use auto layout for trees, rings and grids.

s: Import draw.io, Mermaid and outlines; export PNG, SVG, draw.io or JSON; show a board inside a page.
x: Import: draw.io files, Doceo JSON, images, Mermaid flowcharts and indented outlines. Export from the board’s menu. In a page type /diagram to embed a board, or /diagram-from-headings to turn the page’s headings into a mind map.

t: Import from Markdown, Obsidian, Notion and Confluence
s: Folders or .zip exports become folders, pages, links and images.
x: Press + on All notes → Import… (or right-click a folder → Import into this folder…, or Settings → Your files). Choose a folder or .zip. Doceo guesses the tool; you can pick it yourself. Check the summary and press Import. Your originals are never changed; everything lands in one new folder.

t: Link a folder of Markdown files
s: Keep a Doceo folder in step with a folder of .md files — an Obsidian vault, a Git notes repo or anything you edit in another app.
x: Right-click a folder → Link to a Markdown folder…, choose the folder on your computer and press Link. Every .md file becomes a page (sub-folders become folders); every page already in the Doceo folder gets a file. After that, changes go both ways while Doceo is open — when you open it, when the window gets focus, every 20 seconds and a moment after you edit. Settings → Your files → Markdown folders has Sync now, Show and Unlink. Page names are file names: renaming a page renames its file; moving a page to another folder moves the file. A file you rename outside stays the same page. Delete a pa

s: Save a folder as Markdown, HTML or a ready-to-upload website.
x: Right-click a folder → Export folder…, or use Space home → Export. Markdown keeps front matter and relative links; Website adds a menu tree and search.

s: Copy the data folder.
x: Settings → Your files → Open folder. Copy it to a safe place; on a new computer put it in the same location.

s: Add contacts in Settings → People, then use them everywhere.
x: @-mention a person in a page, assign them a task, make them a page owner or an event attendee. A person’s card lists their open tasks, pages and meetings.

s: A phone-sized app with Dashboard, Notes, Calendar and Tasks tabs.
x: Swipe a note or task for quick actions; press and hold for the full menu. Notes open in the quick editor; Page view is for the desktop. Local notifications remind you of events, tasks and reminders (••• → Notifications).

s: Appearance, Tabs & navigation, Calendar, People, Notifications, Tasks, Features, Documents, Updates, Your files and Reset.
x: Ctrl+, opens Settings. Notifications: allow alerts and choose which ones — events (and how long before), meetings starting, tasks due, note reminders, a morning briefing, an overdue nudge, and sound. Doceo sends them while it is open; whatever came due while it was closed is in the bell. “Send a test” shows what they look like. Updates: “Check for updates” asks the website for a newer version; Install downloads it, checks its signature and restarts. Doceo also checks about once a day and tells you; it never installs by itself. Tasks: choose how many days finished tasks stay before they are arc

s: A save failed (disk full, folder missing, permissions).
x: Free some space or check the data folder in Settings → Your files. Keep editing: the banner clears by itself after the next successful save.

s: If a data file can’t be read, Doceo renames it to “.corrupt”, keeps it, and tells you in a banner.
x: Open the data folder and look for files ending in .corrupt. Restore from your backup or send the file with your report.

s: The installers are not code-signed yet.
x: macOS: right-click the app → Open the first time. Windows: More info → Run anyway.

s: Use “Report a problem” at the bottom of this page.
x: Press “Copy details” first and paste them into the report.
